assets.description:
### What is gold, and why is it considered a safe-haven asset?

When markets turn volatile, many investors shift to assets they perceive as stable. Gold tops that list.

Gold is a physical commodity and monetary metal that has served as a store of value for thousands of years. It’s considered a “safe haven” because it historically retains purchasing power during inflation, political instability, or financial crises. Unlike fiat currencies, gold cannot be printed or debased by central banks. It doesn’t default, it doesn’t rely on a counterparty, and it tends to perform well when trust in the financial system erodes.


### Who controls gold production globally?

No single entity owns the gold market - but production is concentrated.

Gold is mined across the globe, with major producers including China, Russia, Australia, the U.S., and Canada. While governments regulate extraction, most gold mining is conducted by private or public companies like Newmont Corporation, Barrick Gold, and AngloGold Ashanti. Central banks influence reserves and price direction through monetary policy and holdings, but no institution fully controls supply. Production levels depend on geology, mining costs, and geopolitical stability.


### How has gold been used historically as money and a store of value?

Fiat currencies fade. Empires fall. Gold endures.

For over 5,000 years, gold has been used as currency, collateral, and a benchmark for monetary systems. It backed national currencies under the gold standard until the 20th century. Even after being replaced by fiat, gold remained a global store of value. In many cultures, gold jewelry also functions as a form of liquid wealth. Its scarcity, durability, and universality have made it a cross-border monetary reserve throughout history.


### What factors influence the price of gold (inflation, interest rates, demand)?

Gold isn’t just shiny metal - it reacts to macro forces in real time.

Key drivers include inflation expectations, real interest rates, U.S. dollar strength, central bank demand, and geopolitical risk. When inflation rises or interest rates fall, gold tends to strengthen. It also benefits from dollar weakness and flight-to-safety behavior during war or recession. Jewelry demand in countries like India and China, along with ETF inflows and mining supply, adds further short- and long-term price pressure.


### Why do investors buy gold in 2025?

In a world of AI hype, unstable geopolitics, and inflation uncertainty - gold feels familiar.

Investors in 2025 are allocating to gold as a portfolio hedge against rate cuts, debt monetization, and U.S. dollar depreciation. 

Persistent inflation and concerns about financial system fragility have renewed interest in hard assets. Unlike many digital assets, gold has low counterparty risk and high liquidity, especially during global drawdowns. Institutional portfolios often use it to reduce overall volatility.

### How does gold compare to stocks, bonds, and Bitcoin as a hedge?

Not all hedges behave the same - and gold’s track record is longer.

Gold typically holds or gains value when stocks fall, making it a defensive asset. It’s uncorrelated with bonds and often outperforms them during inflationary periods. Compared to Bitcoin, gold is less volatile, more regulated, and historically more trusted by institutions. 

Bitcoin has shown hedge-like qualities during monetary debasement but still trades more like a tech stock. Gold remains the benchmark for traditional risk-off hedging.


### What is tokenized gold, and how does it work?

Physical gold is hard to move - tokenized gold solves that.

Tokenized gold represents digital tokens backed 1:1 by physical gold held in vaults. Projects like PAX Gold (PAXG), Tether Gold (XAUT), and Matrixdock tokenize real gold bars stored in secure custodial facilities. Each token reflects the real-time price of gold and can be traded on blockchains like Ethereum or Tron. These assets bring gold into the crypto ecosystem with easier transferability and lower custody friction.


### Where can I buy tokenized gold (PAXG, Tether Gold, Matrixdock Gold)?

Tokenized gold is available across major crypto platforms.

You can buy PAXG, XAUT, and other tokenized gold assets on centralized exchanges like Binance, Kraken, or Bitfinex. Some DeFi protocols and DEXs on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and other chains also support them via stablecoin pairs. Availability depends on your location and the exchange’s listing policies. These tokens can be stored in self-custody wallets like MetaMask, making gold accessible to crypto-native users.


### Is tokenized gold fully backed by physical gold reserves?

Backing matters - especially when trust is the selling point.

Yes, most reputable tokenized gold assets like PAXG and Tether Gold claim to be fully backed by physical gold bars stored in regulated vaults. Issuers publish audit reports and allow token holders to redeem for actual metal under specific conditions. 

However, redemption policies, jurisdictions, and fees vary. Always verify the custodian details and audit transparency before treating the tokens as equivalent to vault-stored gold.


### How is gold being integrated into DeFi and blockchain ecosystems?

DeFi users want low-volatility collateral - and gold fits.

Tokenized gold is increasingly used in lending, staking, and synthetic asset protocols. Platforms like [Aave] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/aave/) and DeFiChain allow users to borrow against gold tokens or earn yield through liquidity pools. Unlike stablecoins, gold-backed tokens can preserve purchasing power without relying on fiat pegs. Gold also serves as a collateral layer in emerging real-world asset [(RWA)] (https://coinmarketcap.com/real-world-assets/) protocols that aim to tokenize traditional assets in a permissionless way.


### Which blockchains support tokenized gold?

Tokenized gold needs scale and security - and blockchains like Ethereum deliver both.

Ethereum is the most widely used chain for tokenized gold, with projects like [PAXG] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/pax-gold/) and [XAUT] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/tether-gold/) operating as ERC-20 tokens. Tron offers lower fees and supports alternatives like Tether Gold. Other chains such as [BNB Chain] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/bnb/), Polygon, and Avalanche may also list bridged versions of gold tokens. Interoperability protocols and multichain wallets now make it easy to transfer tokenized gold across ecosystems.


### How does tokenized gold compare to [Bitcoin] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/bitcoin/) as “digital gold”?

Bitcoin is called digital gold - but tokenized gold is literally that.

Tokenized gold tracks the physical commodity directly, backed by vault-stored assets. Bitcoin is a decentralized, fixed-supply digital currency often positioned as a long-term inflation hedge. 

While Bitcoin has outperformed gold in recent bull markets, it remains more volatile and unbacked. Tokenized gold offers stability and is easier for traditional institutions to integrate into portfolios. The two assets serve different risk profiles and roles within crypto.


### Why is the price of gold rising (or falling) today?

Gold doesn’t trade on hype - it trades on macro signals.

The price of gold often rises due to falling real interest rates, central bank accumulation, or geopolitical tensions. It may fall when bond yields rise or the U.S. dollar strengthens. Short-term moves can also result from ETF flows or profit-taking after sharp rallies. In recent years, price shifts have increasingly reflected investor views on monetary policy, inflation expectations, and global de-dollarization trends.


### How does gold perform during recessions or stock market crashes?

Gold tends to rise when everything else is falling.

During recessions or market crashes, gold often outperforms both stocks and risk assets. It held value during the 2008 financial crisis, and in early COVID-19 panic, gold recovered faster than equities. It doesn’t pay dividends, but its role as a hedge and store of value typically attracts capital in risk-off cycles. While not immune to drawdowns, gold usually provides relative stability during systemic stress.

### What is Circle Internet Group Inc., and what does the company do?

Circle is a fintech company that builds infrastructure for digital currencies and blockchain-based finance.

Its core product is USDC-a fully-backed stablecoin used for payments, DeFi, trading, and tokenization. Circle also provides APIs, wallets, and treasury services for businesses integrating digital dollars into global operations.


### How is Circle connected to [USDC] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/usd-coin/) (USD Coin)?

Circle is the co-creator and primary issuer of USDC.

Along with Coinbase under the Centre Consortium, Circle helped launch USDC in 2018. It manages reserves, ensures 1:1 backing with U.S. dollars, and facilitates integration with financial institutions and blockchain networks.


### What role does Circle play in the broader crypto and fintech ecosystem?

Circle bridges traditional finance and blockchain.

It powers stablecoin settlement for exchanges, fintech apps, merchants, and DeFi protocols. Circle’s infrastructure enables faster, borderless payments and tokenized dollar rails, making it a key player in Web3 and real-world asset integration.


### Is Circle profitable, and what are its current earnings or projections?

Circle is not yet publicly profitable, but revenue is growing.

The company earns yield on USDC reserves and offers enterprise services. Its IPO was delayed in 2022, but renewed interest in stablecoins and tokenization may strengthen its financial outlook for 2025 and beyond.


### How does Circle’s USDC stablecoin work on the blockchain?

USDC is a fiat-backed stablecoin redeemable 1:1 for U.S. dollars.

Each USDC is backed by cash or short-term U.S. Treasuries, verified via monthly attestations. Users can mint or redeem through Circle or integrated partners, while blockchain wallets freely transfer USDC peer to peer.


### Which blockchains currently support USDC ([Ethereum] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/ethereum/), [Solana] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/solana/) , Polygon, etc.)?

USDC is live on 15+ blockchains.

These include Ethereum, Solana, [Avalanche] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/avalanche/), Polygon, [Arbitrum] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/arbitrum/), Base, [Optimism] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/optimism-ethereum/), [Stellar] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/stellar/), [Near] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/near-protocol/), and more. Circle’s “Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol” also enables seamless movement of USDC across chains with native issuance.


### Could Circle launch more stablecoins (like Euro Coin or others)?

Yes - Circle already launched Euro Coin (EURC).

Backed 1:1 by euros, EURC is Circle’s next step toward multi-currency stablecoin infrastructure. Additional regional fiat stablecoins could follow, especially in response to regulatory clarity and rising global demand.


### Does Circle plan to integrate tokenized real-world assets (RWA) into USDC?

Yes - Circle actively supports the tokenization of RWAs.

USDC serves as settlement and liquidity collateral for tokenized T-bills, treasuries, and private market assets. Circle aims to embed USDC deeper into RWA ecosystems, including partnerships with BlackRock and other asset managers.


### Is Circle stock a good investment for 2025 and beyond?

Circle’s stock may appeal to investors seeking stablecoin and fintech exposure.

If it lists publicly, Circle’s performance will hinge on USDC adoption, regulatory clarity, and its expansion into cross-chain, RWA, and enterprise markets. It's a pure-play bet on tokenized dollars in global finance.


### How is Circle’s USDC different from Tether (USDT)?

USDC is more transparent, but USDT is more widely used.

USDC offers monthly reserve attestations, operates under U.S. oversight, and maintains high-quality collateral. Tether remains dominant in trading volume and global usage but has faced transparency concerns over reserve composition.


### Will Circle benefit from Bitcoin ETFs and crypto adoption?

Yes - more capital inflow into crypto boosts USDC usage.

As Bitcoin ETFs and TradFi adoption expand, demand for fiat on-ramps and stable settlement grows. Circle is well-positioned to serve this demand across exchanges, wallets, and tokenized asset platforms.

### What is MicroStrategy Inc. (MSTR)?

Retail investors seeking Bitcoin exposure via stock often hit roadblocks with ETFs or custody solutions. MicroStrategy solves that by packaging Bitcoin accumulation within a public equity wrapper.

MicroStrategy-rebranded as Strategy™ in early 2025-is a Nasdaq-listed company specializing in business intelligence software while aggressively building Bitcoin reserves. It now identifies as a Bitcoin treasury company, using software revenue and capital markets to fund its crypto strategy.


### Who is the CEO of MicroStrategy, and what is his role in the company’s Bitcoin strategy?

Investors often wonder who drives the strategy behind MSTR’s massive Bitcoin stash.

Michael J. Saylor remains Executive Chairman and the chief architect of the Bitcoin treasury pivot. Phong Le, as President & CEO, handles operations. Saylor oversees capital raises and accumulation of BTC, while Le executes funding strategy and client-facing software services.


### How does MicroStrategy generate revenue?

Traditional software firms earn through software licensing and services-but with MSTR, Bitcoin rules the narrative.

MicroStrategy continues to sell business intelligence software and mobile analytics tools under its legacy brand. On top of that, it leverages Bitcoin by issuing convertible notes, preferred shares, and equity to fund BTC purchases, expecting capital appreciation rather than cash income from crypto.


### How has MSTR performed compared to Bitcoin since 2020?

Traditional investors may not capture the full upside-MSTR often outperforms Bitcoin itself.

From late 2020 to mid‑2025, MSTR stock surged roughly 3,558%, significantly exceeding Bitcoin’s 905% gain during the same period. While BTC appreciation drives the stock, MSTR’s leverage through debt and equity offerings amplifies returns-and volatility.


### Could MicroStrategy tokenize its Bitcoin holdings or offer tokenized shares?

Many expect tokenization from crypto-first firms. Strategy has already taken a bold step.

MicroStrategy’s equity is offered as [tokenized stock] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/microstrategy-tokenized-stock-xstock/), such as MSTRX via xStocks and tokenized MSTR on Gemini (EU). That allows shares to trade on-chain, but BTC holdings themselves are not tokenized. Strategy hasn’t issued a stablecoin or Bitcoin-backed token-it tokenized its own equity only.


### How does MicroStrategy plan to handle Bitcoin price volatility long-term?

Volatility is a feature, not a bug, in Strategy’s model.

While legacy software remains loss-making, Strategy uses capital tools (preferred shares, convertible notes) to fund BTC buys. It holds Bitcoin long-term, betting that appreciation outweighs risk. The company also retains flexibility to issue new equity or debt if needed, treating BTC as a long-duration asset.


### How much Bitcoin does MicroStrategy own today?

Investors tracking BTC exposure need precise numbers-Strategy publishes updates regularly.

As of July 2025, Strategy holds 601,550 BTC, acquired at an average cost of ~$71,268 per coin, with a total cost basis near $42.9 billion. The holdings are valued at over $73 billion based on current price, representing about 3% of all Bitcoin in circulation.


### Can you buy MicroStrategy tokenized shares on a blockchain?

Investors may look for equity tokens-yes, they exist for MSTR.

Tokenized versions such as MSTRX and FTX-based MSTR tokenized stock are available on platforms like xStocks and Gemini for EU users. These trade 24/7 and allow fractional ownership via stablecoins or crypto wallets.


### What are the biggest risks of investing in MicroStrategy stock?

Investing in MSTR means not just equity risk, but crypto and financing risk.

Key risks include Bitcoin price crashes, rising leverage costs, ESG and regulatory backlash, and software business underperformance. Token dilution from arrests of capital raises or preferred offerings may further pressure MSTR in bear markets.


### Is MicroStrategy more of a Bitcoin ETF proxy or a traditional software company?

It began as software, but today it behaves more like a Bitcoin ETF proxy.

While Strategy still sells BI software, its identity and valuation now derive primarily from Bitcoin holdings. Analysts view it as a leveraged, publicly traded proxy for BTC exposure-far removed from SaaS or mobile app revenue streams.

assets.name: Nvidia Corp
assets.description:
###  What is NVIDIA, and when was it founded?

New investors often associate NVIDIA with gaming, but its reach goes far beyond graphics cards.

NVIDIA is a U.S.-based semiconductor and computing company specializing in GPUs, AI hardware, and high-performance computing. It was founded in 1993 in California and became publicly traded in 1999 under the ticker NVDA. Originally built for the gaming market, NVIDIA now powers global AI models, cloud data centers, autonomous vehicles, and industrial simulations. Its rapid expansion into data infrastructure has redefined its role in modern computing.


###  Who founded NVIDIA, and who is its current CEO?

The personalities behind tech companies often get overlooked - until they dominate entire sectors.

NVIDIA was founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem. Huang has served as CEO since the company’s inception and remains its public face and strategic leader. His deep engineering background and long-term vision have been central to NVIDIA’s rise from a GPU provider to a global AI infrastructure firm. His leadership is widely credited for navigating multiple market pivots.


###  Who owns NVIDIA today? Who are the company’s largest shareholders?

Retail investors often miss who’s really moving the stock behind the scenes - institutions.

NVIDIA is a publicly traded company owned by a mix of institutional investors and retail shareholders. Its largest holders include investment giants like Vanguard, BlackRock, and Fidelity. Jensen Huang also owns a significant personal stake. Institutions control a majority of the float, giving them outsized influence over price movements, especially during earnings cycles or broader tech sell-offs.

###  How did NVIDIA become a leader in AI, GPUs, and data centers?

Most companies don’t survive one pivot. NVIDIA nailed multiple.

NVIDIA built dominance in the gaming GPU market, but its real edge came from repurposing GPUs for general-purpose computing. This made it ideal for training neural networks and building AI models. Over time, NVIDIA invested in CUDA (its developer platform), data center hardware, and AI chips like the H100. This ecosystem approach gave it a monopoly-like position in AI computing, powering everything from ChatGPT to Tesla’s AI training clusters.


###  What industries rely most on NVIDIA’s products?

Many assume NVIDIA only powers games. In reality, it runs some of the world’s most complex systems.

Industries using NVIDIA include AI research, autonomous vehicles, robotics, gaming, defense, pharmaceuticals, and finance. Its chips are foundational for training and deploying machine learning models, which makes it essential to cloud computing platforms and supercomputers. Hospitals, universities, and energy companies increasingly depend on its hardware for simulations and data analysis.


###  What is NVIDIA’s roadmap for AI, autonomous vehicles, and the metaverse?

NVIDIA doesn’t build consumer apps - it builds the platforms they run on.

Its roadmap includes high-efficiency chips like the Blackwell architecture for large-scale AI, AI factories for model training, and Drive platforms for autonomous vehicles. NVIDIA also powers 3D virtual environments through its Omniverse platform, designed to simulate real-world factories, workflows, and digital twins. It is not competing with OpenAI or Meta - it's building the infrastructure they all rely on.


###  What role will NVIDIA play in future blockchain and crypto infrastructure?

While some chipmakers avoided crypto, NVIDIA played a different game.

NVIDIA’s GPUs have historically powered crypto mining, especially for Ethereum before its shift to proof-of-stake. Today, its main role is likely to emerge in AI x blockchain applications - such as decentralized compute, zk-proofs, and data-heavy blockchain simulations. NVIDIA’s chips are also used in validating cryptographic models and running complex smart contracts on off-chain AI layers.


###  What is NVIDIA’s current stock price, and why is it moving today?

Price alone doesn’t tell the story - you need context.

NVIDIA’s stock price changes daily based on market sentiment, earnings expectations, and broader tech trends. Short-term price moves are often tied to AI-related news, analyst upgrades, or macroeconomic data like inflation or interest rate changes. NVDA is also a major component of tech indexes, so ETF flows can drive volume up or down without company-specific catalysts.


###  Is NVIDIA stock a good buy for long-term investors?

Retail traders often focus on hype cycles - but long-term returns depend on structural trends.

NVIDIA offers exposure to long-term growth in AI, cloud computing, and robotics. Its competitive moat in chip architecture, developer tools, and infrastructure gives it strong pricing power. That said, it trades at a premium valuation, and any slowdown in AI infrastructure spending could trigger a correction. For long-term investors with a high risk tolerance, it’s seen as a core bet on the future of computing.


###  Why is NVIDIA stock so volatile?

High-growth tech stocks often have explosive upside - and equally sharp corrections.

NVIDIA’s volatility stems from its valuation multiples, reliance on AI infrastructure spending, and concentrated ownership by large institutions. The stock reacts sharply to earnings beats or misses and is also sensitive to geopolitical issues related to chip exports. 

Traders also use NVDA for options strategies, which amplifies short-term price swings during events like earnings or product launches.


###  What is tokenized NVIDIA stock, and how does it work?

Buying traditional stocks via brokerage isn’t always accessible - tokenized assets offer a workaround.

[Tokenized NVIDIA] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/nvidia-tokenized-stock-xstock/) stock is a digital asset that mirrors the price of NVDA shares. These tokens are typically offered by platforms that hold real shares in custody or replicate their value synthetically. Users can trade them 24/7 on blockchain platforms, often using stablecoins. 

However, tokenized stocks don’t always come with voting rights or dividend access and depend heavily on the issuing platform’s credibility.


###  Where can I buy tokenized NVIDIA stock on the blockchain?

Not all tokenized stocks are available everywhere - and regulation plays a big role.

Tokenized NVIDIA shares are available on select crypto platforms like Uphold, Mirror Protocol (historically), or Synthetix. Some centralized exchanges also experiment with synthetic equity offerings. These platforms often require KYC and may restrict access based on jurisdiction. 

Always verify whether the token is legally backed or synthetic before trading.


###  Is tokenized NVIDIA (NVDA) backed 1:1 by real shares?

Not all tokenized assets are equal - backing matters.

Some platforms offer tokenized NVDA fully backed by real shares held in custody. Others provide synthetic versions that only mirror the price without holding underlying assets. Backed tokens are more likely to reflect actual shareholder rights, while synthetic tokens rely on smart contracts and liquidity providers. Always check the platform’s documentation and custodial agreements before assuming parity with traditional stocks.


###  Will NVIDIA’s growth in AI continue to push its stock higher?

AI hype alone can’t sustain valuations - execution matters.

NVIDIA is well-positioned to benefit from expanding AI demand, especially in training infrastructure. However, growth will depend on whether customers like hyperscalers and AI labs continue investing at current levels. The stock’s performance also hinges on new chip architectures, competitive pricing, and government policies on chip exports. If the AI buildout slows or competition intensifies, growth expectations may be revised downward.


###  What are the biggest risks for NVIDIA investors in 2025?

High-growth stocks carry asymmetrical risk - and NVIDIA is no exception.

Key risks include dependency on a small set of AI clients, regulatory limits on chip exports (especially to China), and rising competition from AMD, Intel, or custom chips built in-house by major cloud providers. Geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, and AI spending slowdowns could also hit revenue. Lastly, valuation risk looms - if future growth doesn’t meet expectations, corrections could be sharp.

### What is Tesla, who founded it, who is the current CEO and when was it founded?

Retail investors often assume Elon Musk started Tesla-but the story is more complex.

Tesla was founded in July 2003 by engineers Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning. Elon Musk joined later as lead investor and became CEO in 2008. Under Musk, Tesla evolved from a niche EV startup into a dominant player in electric vehicles, energy storage, and autonomous driving.


### What are analysts forecasting for Tesla’s growth by 2030?

Tesla’s valuation depends heavily on what the next decade looks like-not just current sales.

By 2030, some analysts forecast Tesla delivering 10–20 million vehicles annually, up from ~1.8 million in 2023. Growth is expected from energy storage, robotaxis, and full self-driving software. Bullish models project a market cap exceeding $2 trillion if margins hold and new business lines scale .


### Is Tesla stock available as a tokenized asset on the blockchain?

Yes - Tesla is one of the most actively traded tokenized equities.

Tokenized TSLA is offered on select crypto platforms and mirrors the price of the real stock. These assets are typically backed 1:1 with TSLA shares held by a custodian or operate synthetically via decentralized protocols.


### How can investors trade Tesla tokenized stock through crypto exchanges?

You don’t need a brokerage to get exposure to [TSLA] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/tesla-tokenized-stock-xstock/).

Platforms like Uphold, Synthetix, and formerly FTX have offered Tesla tokens. Investors can trade them against stablecoins, often with 24/7 access. Some exchanges require KYC, while others allow limited access via DeFi apps or wrapped tokens.


### Has Tesla invested in cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin or others?

Tesla made headlines when it put Bitcoin on its balance sheet.

In 2021, Tesla bought $1.5 billion worth of [Bitcoin] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/bitcoin/) and briefly accepted BTC for car purchases. The company later sold a portion of its holdings but still holds Bitcoin as part of its treasury strategy.


### How do Tesla’s Bitcoin holdings affect its stock performance?

Even a modest Bitcoin allocation can move the stock.

Because Tesla publicly holds Bitcoin, its stock price sometimes reacts to BTC volatility. This effect is more pronounced during sharp crypto market moves or when Tesla discloses buys or sells in its earnings reports.


### Is Tesla considering blockchain technology for supply chain or energy solutions?

While Tesla hasn’t announced large blockchain integrations, it's exploring the tech.

There are ongoing experiments in using blockchain for renewable energy credits, supply chain verification, and charging infrastructure data. Tesla’s energy division could benefit from decentralized tracking of solar production and battery sharing networks.


### Can Tesla’s tokenized stock be staked or used in DeFi protocols?

Yes, but with caveats. Some tokenized versions of TSLA are compatible with DeFi platforms. 

They can be staked, borrowed against, or added to liquidity pools. However, this depends on the platform (e.g., Mirror, Synthetix) and whether the token is synthetic or backed by real equity.


### How does Tesla’s involvement in crypto impact its valuation?

Crypto exposure adds volatility-and optionality. Tesla’s crypto activity has attracted digital-native investors and made the stock part of macro Bitcoin narratives. While not core to its valuation, BTC exposure creates asymmetric headlines and speculative upside that traditional automakers lack.


### How has Tesla stock performed over the last 5 years?

Tesla has delivered massive long-term gains-despite frequent volatility.

From mid-2020 to mid-2025, TSLA has seen a roughly 600–800% return, depending on split-adjusted timing. These gains reflect expansion into China, new Gigafactories, Model Y dominance, and increasing investor confidence in AI and energy storage segments.


### What is the Tesla stock price prediction for 2025 and beyond?

Forecasts range widely depending on growth assumptions.

By 2025, bulls expect TSLA to exceed $350–$400 per share, driven by software margins and autonomy breakthroughs. Bearish models price it around $180–$220, citing EV competition, margin pressure, and delays in robotaxi timelines.


### How can I buy Tesla stock or tokenized TSLA?

You can go traditional or crypto-native.

Buy TSLA directly through brokerages like Robinhood, Fidelity, or Interactive Brokers. For crypto users, tokenized TSLA is available on platforms like Uphold, Synthetix, or other DeFi protocols-just verify if the token is synthetic or custodian-backed.

### What is Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN)?

Retail investors often struggle with fragmented crypto platforms. Coinbase solves this by providing an all‑in‑one, regulated exchange and wallet ecosystem.

Coinbase Global is a U.S.-listed company that operates one of the largest crypto trading platforms worldwide. It offers retail and institutional services, including spot trading, staking, wallets, custody, payment infrastructure, and stablecoin support.


### Who founded Coinbase, and when was it created?

Many platforms lack clear origin stories. Coinbase's founders built it with trust and regulatory compliance front and center.

[Coinbase] (https://coinmarketcap.com/exchanges/coinbase-exchange/) was founded in June 2012 by Brian Armstrong and Fred Ehrsam. Armstrong previously worked at Airbnb and launched Coinbase via Y Combinator. Ehrsam joined after his experience at Goldman Sachs brought financial and blockchain insight to the team.


### How has Coinbase stock performed since its IPO?

Crypto volatility makes COIN hard to benchmark. But its stock has mirrored Bitcoin’s cycles.

Coinbase went public in April 2021 via direct listing with an $85 billion valuation. Its shares soared early, then fell sharply in 2022 as crypto prices tanked. Since then, the stock has partially recovered-gaining 40‑50 percent in 2024–2025 amid renewed crypto optimism and regulatory clarity.


### What factors influence Coinbase’s share price the most?

COIN is sensitive to crypto market moods, not economic indicators.

The share price moves in tandem with Bitcoin and ether prices, overall trading volume, and crypto market sentiment. Institutional adoption, new regulatory frameworks (e.g., stablecoin legislation), and product launches-like stablecoin-based payments-also drive price shifts.


### What is Coinbase’s future roadmap for growth in crypto markets?

Investors need clarity on sustainable fees and product innovation. Coinbase is evolving beyond spot trading.

The company plans to expand stablecoin payments, custody solutions, crypto derivatives, Prime brokerage, and institutional onboarding. Its acquisition of Deribit aims to grow options and futures trading. Coinbase also focuses on institutional products like staking, derivatives, and USDC revenue-sharing with Circle.


### How is Coinbase adapting to increasing crypto regulation?

Lack of crypto regulation adds operational uncertainty. Coinbase faces it head-on with compliance-first strategy.

Coinbase has actively lobbied for bills like the GENIUS Act and Clarity Act to clarify stablecoin and crypto rules. It maintains strong KYC/AML controls, supports U.S. regulatory dialogue, and operates with legal defense posture-securing dismissal of an SEC lawsuit in 2025.

Apple Inc. is a U.S.-based technology company that designs consumer electronics, software, and services. It was founded by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne in 1976.

Initially focused on personal computers, Apple's scope has expanded significantly, and it's now considered one of the most influential companies in the world. Many investors assume Apple's success is tied entirely to iPhone sales, but its revenue model is broader than it looks.

Beyond the iPhone, Apple sells Mac computers, iPads, and wearable devices like the Apple Watch and AirPods. It also operates major software and services platforms including iCloud, Apple Music, Apple Pay, and the App Store. While many tech firms rush AI to market, Apple tends to move slower - but with more control and deeper integration.

Apple uses AI across its ecosystem, from Siri voice recognition to photo organization, battery optimization, and on-device predictive text. Apple Pay, for example, can be linked to such cards, allowing crypto-funded purchases in Apple Stores or online. Day-to-day price action can feel random. But short-term spikes often reflect clear catalysts.

### What is Robinhood Markets Inc., and what services does it provide?

New investors often feel priced out or overwhelmed by legacy trading platforms. Robinhood removes this barrier by offering commission-free access to stocks, [ETFs] (https://coinmarketcap.com/etf/), crypto, and options through a mobile-first interface.

Founded on democratizing finance, Robinhood enables users to trade small amounts with no minimums. It also offers a crypto wallet, real-time market data, and educational tools tailored for beginners. Its design emphasizes simplicity, making it appealing to digital natives.

Robinhood's platform is widely used by Gen Z and millennial investors looking to build portfolios without traditional brokerage complexity. Its expansion into crypto has made it one of the most accessible trading platforms for both equities and digital assets.


### When was Robinhood founded, and who were its founders?

In 2013, Stanford graduates Vladimir Tenev and Baiju Bhatt launched Robinhood with a bold mission-make trading accessible to everyone. The founders saw that traditional brokerages were charging high fees and lacked transparency.

They built a platform that gave users direct access to financial markets, starting with stocks and ETFs, then later expanding to options and crypto. The company officially launched its app in 2015, gaining traction with younger investors who wanted a simpler way to participate in markets.

Their vision of “democratizing finance” resonated at a time when retail investors were seeking alternatives to Wall Street gatekeepers.


### How did Robinhood disrupt traditional stock and crypto trading?

Most brokerages charged $5–$10 per trade before Robinhood. By eliminating trading commissions, Robinhood forced the entire industry to lower fees or go commission-free.

It also replaced complex trading interfaces with an intuitive mobile app, opening the market to first-time investors. For crypto, Robinhood simplified access by allowing users to buy major coins like Bitcoin and Ethereum without needing wallets or blockchain knowledge.

This disruption wasn’t just about price-it was about accessibility. The platform lowered the technical and financial barriers that kept retail investors on the sidelines.


### How does Robinhood make money (commissions, payment for order flow, etc.)?

Robinhood doesn’t charge for trades, but it still earns revenue through indirect channels. Its primary income comes from payment for order flow-routing trades to market makers who pay for the order volume.

It also earns interest on uninvested customer cash, margin loans through Robinhood Gold, and fees on crypto transactions.

This model aligns with Robinhood’s goal of providing free trading, but it has sparked regulatory scrutiny over transparency and best execution practices. Still, it remains one of the most profitable zero-commission platforms globally.


### How did Robinhood’s role in the GameStop/AMC short squeeze impact its reputation?

During the January 2021 retail trading frenzy, Robinhood restricted trading on GameStop, AMC, and other volatile stocks. This decision triggered a backlash from users and lawmakers who accused the company of siding with institutional players.

Robinhood said the move was due to clearinghouse collateral requirements-not to protect hedge funds. Still, the incident sparked class-action lawsuits, Congressional hearings, and long-term trust issues.

The short squeeze highlighted Robinhood’s systemic limitations and exposed the fragility of “free trading” during times of extreme volatility.


### Is Robinhood (HOOD) stock a good long-term investment?

Robinhood stock offers exposure to a younger, fast-growing user base in both traditional finance and crypto. But its growth relies heavily on market volatility and trading volumes, which are unpredictable.

Analysts are split. Bulls see upside in crypto expansion, international growth, and possible subscription revenue. Bears point to regulatory risks, slowing user growth, and dependence on PFOF.

For long-term investors, HOOD is a high-risk/high-reward play. It’s best suited for those who believe Robinhood can evolve beyond trading and into a full-service financial platform.


### Is Robinhood profitable, and when is it expected to be consistently profitable?

Robinhood has had a few profitable quarters, but consistent profitability remains elusive. Its revenues fluctuate with trading activity, especially in crypto.

In 2023 and early 2024, Robinhood cut costs and leaned into subscription services like Robinhood Gold. It also expanded into new markets and products, including retirement accounts and IRAs.

Analysts expect profitability to stabilize as revenue diversifies, but volatility in user activity could delay that timeline.


### How is Robinhood integrating cryptocurrency trading into its business model?

Robinhood has steadily added crypto to its core business. Users can buy and sell major cryptocurrencies alongside stocks in a single app.

The company launched a self-custody crypto wallet, allowing users to withdraw, store, and transfer tokens directly. It also offers on-chain swaps via DeFi protocols and integrates security features like wallet backup and biometric verification.

Crypto now contributes a sizable portion of Robinhood’s transaction revenue, especially during bull markets.


### Could Robinhood stock be tokenized and traded on blockchain platforms?

Robinhood itself hasn’t issued tokenized shares, but third-party platforms offer synthetic or tokenized versions of HOOD stock. 

These tokens track the price of the underlying stock and are often backed 1:1 by real shares held by custodians.

Such tokenized assets can be traded 24/7 on decentralized platforms, unlike traditional markets. However, availability varies by jurisdiction, and liquidity may be limited.

Investors should check regulatory compliance and collateral backing before using tokenized HOOD products.


### How is Robinhood competing in the crypto trading space with Binance and Coinbase?

Robinhood differentiates itself through simplicity, not depth. Unlike Coinbase or Binance, Robinhood offers fewer coins but a smoother UI, fee-free crypto trades (built into spreads), and integration with stock trading.

Its self-custody wallet adds DeFi access, closing the feature gap. However, Robinhood still lags in advanced trading tools, staking, and altcoin support.

Its edge is regulatory positioning-being a U.S.-based public company helps it win trust with regulators and traditional investors.


### Can Robinhood stock itself be purchased as a tokenized asset on DeFi platforms?

Yes, tokenized versions of HOOD are offered by platforms like Synthetix or Mirror Protocol, though availability can vary. These synthetic assets mirror the price of Robinhood stock and may be used in DeFi for lending, trading, or staking.

But they don’t always offer voting rights or dividends, and they rely on oracle systems or custodians for price tracking.

Due diligence is critical. Tokenized stocks on DeFi platforms are not always backed by real shares.


### Could Robinhood launch its own crypto token or blockchain network?

Robinhood hasn’t announced plans for a native token or proprietary blockchain. Its focus remains on offering secure, regulated access to existing crypto ecosystems.

Launching a token would create regulatory complications, especially in the U.S., where securities law applies broadly.

Still, Robinhood could expand into stablecoins, Layer 2 integrations, or DeFi APIs through its wallet infrastructure. That would deepen its role in the Web3 stack without creating regulatory friction.


### How can investors buy tokenized Robinhood stock?

[Tokenized HOOD] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/robinhood-tokenized-stock-xstock/) is available on select platforms like FTX (before its collapse), Synthetix, or Binance through derivatives. These tokens typically represent real shares held by a custodian or use synthetic price tracking.

Investors need a crypto wallet, often USDC or BUSD to trade, and access to a DeFi or centralized exchange that lists the asset.
Trading fees, spreads, and availability vary. Always verify the asset’s collateralization and issuer credibility.


### Is Robinhood expanding its crypto wallet and DeFi services?

Yes. Robinhood launched a multi-chain self-custody wallet in 2023, adding support for Ethereum, Polygon, and Bitcoin. The wallet enables token swaps, dApp interaction, and cross-chain transfers.

Users can access DeFi protocols directly, bypassing custodial risk. Robinhood continues to expand supported tokens and explore staking and NFT integrations.

This wallet ecosystem positions Robinhood as more than just a centralized exchange. It’s gradually becoming a hybrid crypto on-ramp and DeFi gateway.


### Could Robinhood face regulatory risks impacting its stock price?

Yes. Robinhood’s business model-especially PFOF and crypto-faces ongoing scrutiny from the SEC and state regulators.
Any changes to how brokers can route trades or custody crypto could impact revenue streams and user acquisition.

Additionally, if Congress tightens retail investing rules following events like the GameStop saga, it could slow user growth.
For investors, regulatory clarity or setbacks can move HOOD stock sharply in either direction.

### Who founded Walmart, and who is the current CEO?

Investors often overlook the origins of retail giants when evaluating long-term value. Walmart's story is key to understanding its strategy.

Walmart was founded in 1962 by Sam Walton, who focused on offering low prices in rural American towns. That early cost-leadership strategy remains central to the company today.

As of 2024, Doug McMillon is the President and CEO of Walmart Inc. He has held the role since 2014 and has prioritized eCommerce, supply chain modernization, and international expansion.


### How many stores does Walmart operate globally?

The scale of a retailer directly impacts its supply chain leverage and pricing power.

Walmart operates over 10,500 stores worldwide across formats including supercenters, discount stores, neighborhood markets, and warehouse clubs. These are spread across the U.S., Mexico, Chile, China, Canada, and several other countries.

Its global physical presence supports its logistics, same-day delivery, and last-mile fulfillment infrastructure.


### What are Walmart’s key business segments (e.g., Sam’s Club, eCommerce)?

Understanding Walmart’s business lines helps investors assess where growth is coming from.

Walmart’s core segments include Walmart U.S. (retail and online), Walmart International (retail and wholesale in non-U.S. markets), and Sam’s Club (a U.S.-based warehouse club offering bulk goods).

It also reports a growing eCommerce segment that includes online groceries, marketplace sellers, digital advertising, and financial services.


### What are the main risks to investing in Walmart?

Retailers with thin margins are highly exposed to external shocks.

Walmart faces risks from inflation, wage pressure, and supply chain disruptions. Competition from Amazon and discount grocers also compresses margins. Its international operations introduce regulatory, currency, and political risks.

Despite its scale, Walmart still depends on low-margin, high-volume retail — leaving little room for error in execution.


### How is Walmart expanding its digital and eCommerce operations?

Retail investors want to know whether legacy companies can adapt to online-first economies.

Walmart has been heavily investing in eCommerce through curbside pickup, fulfillment centers, last-mile delivery, and a third-party marketplace. It has also acquired tech startups and developed its own Walmart+ subscription to compete with Amazon Prime.

Digital advertising and financial services are emerging as high-margin additions to its online business.


### Can I buy tokenized Walmart stock on the blockchain?

Access to U.S. equities can be limited in emerging markets. Tokenized stocks aim to solve that.

Yes, tokenized versions of Walmart (WMT) stock are available on select DeFi and synthetic asset platforms. These blockchain-based tokens mirror the real-time price of WMT and allow global, fractional access 24/7.

However, ownership rights may differ from traditional shares.


### Which platforms offer Walmart (WMT) as a tokenized asset?

Access depends on the platform’s approach to tokenization and regulation.

WMT is available as a tokenized asset on protocols like Synthetix, Mirror Protocol (wrapped/synthetic assets), and some custodial platforms like Swarm or Backed. These platforms issue tokens that track Walmart’s price through oracles or are backed by real shares held in custody.

Token availability may be restricted based on jurisdiction.


### How do tokenized Walmart shares work?

Tokenized stocks are not the same as direct equity ownership, and understanding the difference matters.

There are two models: synthetic tokens use decentralized price feeds (e.g., via [Chainlink] (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/chainlink/) ) to mirror WMT's price. Custodial models issue blockchain tokens backed 1:1 by actual Walmart shares held by a regulated entity.

These tokens trade on-chain, may allow fractional ownership, and settle instantly — but typically lack shareholder rights or dividends.


### Is Walmart using blockchain for supply chain management?

Investors looking for enterprise blockchain adoption often focus on logistics-heavy industries.

Walmart is one of the earliest corporate adopters of blockchain for supply chain tracking. It uses Hyperledger-based solutions to trace food products like lettuce and pork across suppliers, reducing fraud and improving safety.

Walmart’s blockchain use is focused on efficiency, compliance, and traceability — not public chains or tokens.


### How can I invest in Walmart — traditional or tokenized shares?

Retail investors want exposure to large-cap equities but may lack access or flexibility.

Walmart shares trade on the NYSE under the ticker WMT, available through brokers like Fidelity, Robinhood, or eToro. Tokenized versions are accessible via synthetic asset platforms and some DeFi protocols, offering 24/7 trading, fractional units, and broader accessibility.

Each method comes with different legal protections, tax implications, and counterparty risk. Choose based on jurisdiction, use case, and custody preference.

### What are the key business divisions of UnitedHealth Group?

Investors often overlook how diversified healthcare companies actually make money. UnitedHealth splits its operations into two high-performing engines.

UnitedHealthcare is the insurance arm, covering individuals, employers, and governments. It generates revenue through premiums and care management. Optum, on the other hand, includes three units: OptumHealth (clinical services), OptumInsight (data and tech), and OptumRx (pharmacy benefit management).

This structure enables UnitedHealth to serve nearly every part of the U.S. healthcare system, from claims to clinics.


### What are UnitedHealth’s main sources of revenue?

Understanding how healthcare giants earn is essential in assessing risk. UnitedHealth’s revenue is split between premium income and service-based models.

UnitedHealthcare drives most of the revenue through insurance premiums from commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid plans. Optum contributes significantly through pharmacy services, tech platforms, data analytics, and direct healthcare delivery.

This dual-income stream allows UnitedHealth to remain stable across economic cycles and policy shifts.


### Does UnitedHealth pay dividends?

Some healthcare stocks are strong on growth but weak on income. UnitedHealth provides both.

Yes, UnitedHealth Group pays quarterly dividends and has consistently increased its payout over the years. While not a high-yield stock, the dividend reflects stable cash flows and a mature business model.

It appeals to long-term investors who want a mix of capital appreciation and predictable returns.


### What are the main risks to investing in UnitedHealth?

Healthcare stocks come with unique challenges, and UnitedHealth is no exception.

Major risks include policy changes that impact insurance margins, regulatory scrutiny over data use, and rising medical costs that could compress profits. Additionally, government contract dependencies (especially Medicare Advantage) pose long-term exposure to legislative shifts.

Operational complexity also creates risk if any business unit underperforms or faces disruption.


### What is UnitedHealth’s strategy for long-term growth?

Investors want to know if a company can scale sustainably without relying on just one market. UnitedHealth’s answer is vertical integration.

Its strategy focuses on combining insurance, clinical care, and data under one ecosystem. Optum is leading this push by acquiring clinics, expanding digital tools, and managing population health.

UnitedHealth sees growth not just in adding members but in controlling the full patient journey — from diagnosis to delivery.

assets.description:
### What is DeFi Development Corp (DFDV), and what does the company do?

Retail investors often lack exposure to crypto-native equity that aligns with digital asset growth. DeFi Development Corp fills that gap.

DFDV is a Nasdaq-listed company that builds value via a SOL-denominated treasury strategy. It accumulates and stakes Solana (SOL), operates validator nodes like Dogwifhat, and manages staking partnerships, generating on-chain income tied to SOL growth. It targets investors who want stock exposure aligned with crypto-native capital allocation.


### Is DeFi Development Corp purely a DeFi/blockchain company, or does it have traditional finance operations?

Some investors mistake DFDV for a fintech or prop tech firm. But it's fully crypto-native in business strategy.

Though formerly part of real estate fintech (as Janover), since April 2025 DFDV rebranded and now focuses solely on crypto treasury accumulation, validator income, and DeFi protocol participation. There is no core traditional finance operation apart from public equity listing and capital markets access.


### Does DeFi Development Corp have a native token or blockchain protocol?

Investors often expect public blockchain tokens from crypto-linked stocks. DFDV doesn't issue a native token.

However, the company launched a tokenized version of its equity-DFDVx-on the Solana network, tradable via Kraken’s xStocks platform. DFDVx allows equity-like trading on-chain but is not a blockchain protocol or design-token structure.


### How does DeFi Development Corp generate revenue from its DeFi platforms?

Cash flow for DFDV hinges on staking income and treasury appreciation.

 The company stakes Solana via validator operations (like Dogwifhat) and shares net rewards with partners after costs. It also earns yield on SOL reserves, including liquid-staked derivatives (e.g., Sanctum). As SOL prices rise or staking rewards compound, DFDV’s asset base-and potential stock value-grows.


### Is DeFi Development Corp (DFDV) stock a good long-term investment?

DFDV is not a traditional growth stock-it's a play on Solana exposure via equity.

Investors who expect Solana to increase in value and staking demand to expand may benefit. Price action will depend heavily on SOL performance, staking flow, tokenization adoption, and regulatory clarity. For risk-seeking investors aligned with Solana, DFDV offers a unique equity proxy-though volatility can be extreme.


### Could regulatory changes impact DeFi Development Corp’s stock price?

Yes - DFDV’s model relies on compliance with both securities and digital asset rules.

Changes in regulation of staking income treatment, tokenized equity frameworks, or crypto taxation could impact how DFDV operates or qualifies as a U.S.-listed firm. Regulatory shifts around tokenized shares could also affect liquidity or issuance of DFDVx on platforms like Kraken.


### Can investors trade DeFi Development Corp stock as a tokenized asset on DeFi platforms?

Yes - DFDV offers DFDVx, a tokenized equity version of its Nasdaq stock, live on Solana.
 
DFDVx trades on Kraken’s xStocks platform, allowing 24/7 on-chain trading and integration into DeFi protocols. It serves institutional and retail users who prefer digital asset settlement and composability. 


### How does DeFi Development Corp integrate crypto trading or staking into its operations?

DFDV doesn’t offer retail crypto trading directly. Its business is focused on staking and treasury.

The company stakes its SOL holdings via validator partnerships and uses platforms like Sanctum for liquid staking. Tokenized equity (DFDVx) can be used in DeFi protocols for lending or borrowing-but DFDV itself remains a staking infrastructure operator, not a trading exchange.


### How does DFDV benefit from the tokenization of stocks, ETFs, or commodities?

Tokenization opens new liquidity and utility layers for DFDV’s equity.

By issuing DFDVx on Solana, the company enables trading, lending, and composability in DeFi. Developers can build apps around DFDVx, treating equity like programmable money. That creates deeper value capture and on-chain utility beyond traditional stock settlement protocols.


### What role does DeFi Development Corp play in the broader tokenized stock and RWA market?

DFDV is a leading example in tokenized real-world assets (RWA).

It’s the first U.S.-listed “crypto treasury strategy” firm to issue tokenized equity. 

As part of Kraken’s xStocks initial cohort, DFDV is bridging equity markets with DeFi. Its early entrance signals how tokenized stocks could grow into mainstream financial primitives.


### How can investors trade tokenized DFDV stock on decentralized exchanges?

Currently, DFDVx trades via centralized chain-native platforms like Kraken’s xStocks.

Over time, decentralized trading of DFDVx may appear on Solana-based DEXs or DeFi protocols like Raydium or Serum. Integration partners like Mayan aim to enable cross-chain access, expanding where DFDVx can be traded onchain.


### Does DFDV’s DeFi growth strategy include NFTs, tokenized ETFs, or RWA markets?

DFDV's strategy focuses on staked crypto and tokenized equity rather than NFTs or ETFs.

While it participates in the broader RWA movement via tokenized shares and SOL-based treasury assets, it has not launched ETFs or NFT-based platforms. Future expansion could involve building DeFi primitives around DFDVx or partnering in fractionalization of equities or tokenized debt-backed assets.

The additions of the Company Store brought textiles to the lineup, and the 2024 tie-up with SRS will help grow professional demand in roofing, pool and landscaping projects.

assets.name: Lockheed Martin Corp
assets.description: Lockheed Martin is the world's largest defense contractor and has dominated the Western market for high-end fighter aircraft since it won the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter program in 2001. Aeronautics is Lockheed's largest segment, which derives upward of two-thirds of its revenue from the F-35. Lockheed's remaining segments are rotary and mission systems, mainly encompassing the Sikorsky helicopter business; missiles and fire control, which creates missiles and missile defense systems; and space systems, which produces satellites and receives equity income from the United Launch Alliance joint venture.

assets.name: Occidental Petroleum Corp
assets.description: Occidental Petroleum is an independent exploration and production company with operations in the United States, Latin America, and the Middle East. At the end of 2023, the company reported net proved reserves of nearly 4 billion barrels of oil equivalent. Net production averaged 1.327 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2024 at a ratio of roughly 52% oil and natural gas liquids and 48% natural gas.

assets.name: Grab Holdings Ltd
assets.description: Founded in 2012, Grab provides ride-sharing services, food and grocery delivery, and financial services (payments, consumer loans, and enterprise offerings) in eight Southeast-Asian countries through its mobile platform. The company partners with merchants and riders, connecting them with consumers while charging commission to both sides. Grab has a leading market share in and derives 89% of its revenue from its core businesses, ride-sharing and food delivery. Singapore, Indonesia, and Malaysia contributed more than 70% of revenue in 2024. Grab's main competitors in Southeast Asia are Line Man and Goto. Its financial services business is still in its nascent stage and provides minimal revenue currently. The company now also generates advertising revenue.

assets.name: Opendoor Technologies Inc
assets.description: Opendoor Technologies Inc is an end-to-end real estate platform enabling customers to sell and buy a home online. Its product offerings include Sell to Opendoor, its core product where sellers sell their homes directly to the company, and it resells those homes to buyers; List with Opendoor, for customers to list their homes with a partner agent; and Opendoor Marketplace, a capital light marketplace offering that connects home sellers with both institutional and retail buyers. In addition to these products, the company also offers its customers integrated title insurance and escrow services through its subsidiaries. A vast majority of the company's revenue is generated by its core product offering, where it acquires homes directly from sellers and resells those homes to buyers.

assets.name: Medtronic PLC
assets.description: One of the largest medical-device companies, Medtronic develops and manufactures therapeutic medical devices for chronic diseases. Its portfolio includes pacemakers, defibrillators, transcatheter heart valves, stents, insulin pumps, spinal fixation devices, neurovascular products, advanced energy, ablation laser therapy, and surgical tools. The company primarily markets its products to healthcare institutions and physicians in the United States, Western Europe, and Japan. Foreign sales account for roughly 50% of the company's total sales.

assets.name: ON Semiconductor Corp
assets.description: Onsemi is a supplier of power semiconductors and sensors focused on the automotive and industrial markets. Onsemi is the second-largest power chipmaker in the world and the largest supplier of image sensors to the automotive market. While the firm used to be highly vertically integrated, it now pursues a hybrid manufacturing strategy for flexible capacity. Onsemi is pivoting to focus on emerging applications like electric vehicles, autonomous vehicles, industrial automation, and renewable energy.

assets.name: Figure Technology Solutions Inc
assets.description: Figure Technology Solutions Inc is a suite of blockchain-based products and solutions centered around the vision of promoting efficiency and liquidity in financial markets. The company offers a technology-enabled loan origination system and paired this system with a distribution marketplace, Figure Connect, providing access to a deep and broad pool of capital markets partners.

The group produces and sells electricity, capacity, and ancillary services into wholesale U.S. power markets, including PJM and WECC, with its generation fleet located in the Mid-Atlantic and Montana.
